title: Disjoint enumerable sets that cannot be computably separated

based_on.title: Introduction to computability theory
based_on.pages: Chapter5 UCLA course extract, Problem5B.7 p197, exercise statement; explicit uniform first-success proof developed here

summary: Construct disjoint enumerable sets with no computable separator, compare positive disjointification with co-enumerable separation, and identify the role of partial search.
abstract: Suppose two lists of numbers can be generated by programs and never share an entry. Can a program always assign every number to one of two sides, putting the first list on one side and the second on the other? Such a decision procedure need not decide membership in either list, since numbers on neither list may be assigned freely. Nevertheless, some disjoint computably enumerable sets admit no such separation. A diagonal construction gives an explicit pair and a partial computable function whose already defined values cannot be preserved by any total computable function. The situation reverses when nonmembership in each of the two disjoint sets can be recognized: running the two negative searches together always supplies enough information to choose a side. Overlapping positive recognizers can instead be refined into disjoint enumerable alternatives while preserving their union. The distinction is that this refinement makes no total decision outside that union.
